problem:
The position vector $r$ of a particle $P$ (relative to a fixed origin $O$) at time $t$ is given by

$$
r=⟨5{t}^{4}+3,\,\frac{2}{{t}^{2}}⟩,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the velocity vector $v.$

$v=⟨${{field-1}},
{{field-2}}$⟩$
worked_solution:
The particle's velocity vector is given by the derivative of its position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{4}+3),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{2}{{t}^{2}})⟩ \\  & =⟨20{t}^{3},-\frac{4}{{t}^{3}}⟩\end{aligned}
$$
